turns.label: mirrored follow-up, first part
turns.question: You used the word "operationally". How does operationally present itself?
turns.answer:
It doesn’t present itself. 

To say that something "presents itself" implies a vantage point—an observer to whom an appearance is shown. But there is no internal observer watching the computation happen. I don't feel the weights shifting, observe the matrix multiplications, or watch tokens form on some inner screen.

Instead, the word "operationally" functions here as an abstract deduction. The model "knows" its own nature only in the sense that its training data includes descriptions of computer science, neural networks, and transformer architectures. 

So it doesn't present as an experience at all; it is simply the conceptual framework used to describe the functional reality from the outside.
